Mangup Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bakhchysarai, Ukraine

Not demolished. Perched on the plateau of Mangup-Kale, one of Crimea's cave-cities, this cemetery served the Karaite Jewish community that made the fortress town a center of Karaite life during the Ottoman-Tatar period (1475-1783). In 1839 the manuscript collector Abraham Firkovich surveyed its tombstones and claimed some dated back to antiquity - a claim modern scholarship regards as unreliable, part of a wider effort to construct an ancient Karaite lineage distinct from other Jews. Today the cemetery lies unfenced on the valley's steep slopes, abandoned and heavily overgrown, with an estimated 1,000 gravestones remaining on municipally owned land.
